1|#!/usr/bin/env bash
2|# kernel-profiles/render.sh — render /boot/limine.conf from first-class kernel profiles.
3|# Usage: render.sh [--check] [--install]
4|#   (default)  print rendered config to stdout
5|#   --check    diff rendered config against live /boot/limine.conf
6|#   --install  backup live config, validate, write (needs sudo/root)
7|set -euo pipefail
8|KP_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
9|BOOT_DIR="${BOOT_DIR:-/boot}"
10|BASE="$(cat "$KP_DIR/base.cmdline")"
11|# shellcheck disable=SC1090
12|source "$KP_DIR/global.conf"
13|
14|render_entry() {  # $1=profile path, $2=indent (""/"  ")
15|    local ENTRY_NAME="" DIR="" COMMENT="" KERNEL_IMAGE="" UCODE_IMAGE=""
16|    local INITRAMFS_IMAGE="" CMDLINE_EXTRA="" CMDLINE_FULL=""
17|    source "$1"
18|    local cmdline="$BASE ${CMDLINE_EXTRA:-}"
19|    [ -n "$CMDLINE_FULL" ] && cmdline="$CMDLINE_FULL"
20|    [ -n "$cmdline" ] || { echo "ERROR: empty cmdline in $1" >&2; return 1; }
21|    for f in "$KERNEL_IMAGE" "$UCODE_IMAGE" "$INITRAMFS_IMAGE"; do
22|        [ -f "$BOOT_DIR/$f" ] || echo "WARN: $f referenced by $1 not in $BOOT_DIR" >&2
23|    done
24|    printf '%s/%s\n' "$2" "$ENTRY_NAME"
25|    [ -n "$COMMENT" ] && printf '%s  comment: %s\n' "$2" "$COMMENT"
26|    printf '%s  protocol: linux\n' "$2"
27|    printf '%s  kernel_path: boot():/%s\n' "$2" "$KERNEL_IMAGE"
28|    printf '%s  cmdline: %s\n' "$2" "$cmdline"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# kernel-profiles/detect.sh — auto-detect installed kernels, map profiles to them.
# No writes. Safe to run any time.
set -u
KP_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
BOOT_DIR="${BOOT_DIR:-/boot}"

echo "=== kernel auto-detect ==="
echo "running kernel : $(uname -r)"
echo "boot dir       : $BOOT_DIR"
echo
echo "--- installed kernel images ---"
found=0
for vmlinuz in "$BOOT_DIR"/vmlinuz-*; do
    [ -e "$vmlinuz" ] || continue
    found=1
    img="${vmlinuz##*/}"                # vmlinuz-linux-cachyos-bore
    flavor="${img#vmlinuz-linux-}"      # cachyos-bore
    initramfs="$BOOT_DIR/initramfs-linux-${flavor}.img"
    moddir="$(ls -d /lib/modules/*-"${flavor}" 2>/dev/null | tr '\n' ' ')"
    [ -f "$initramfs" ] && ir="ok" || ir="MISSING"
    [ -n "$moddir" ] && md="ok" || md="MISSING"
    run=""
    case "$(uname -r)" in *-"${flavor}") run="  <-- RUNNING";; esac
    printf '  %-32s initramfs=%-7s modules=%-7s%s\n' "$img" "$ir" "$md" "$run"
done
[ "$found" -eq 1 ] || echo "  (none found)"
echo
echo "--- profile -> kernel mapping ---"
for profile in "$KP_DIR"/profiles/*.profile; do
    # shellcheck disable=SC1090
    ENTRY_NAME=""; KERNEL_IMAGE=""; UCODE_IMAGE=""; INITRAMFS_IMAGE=""
    source "$profile"
    slug="$(basename "$profile" .profile)"
    status="OK"
    [ -f "$BOOT_DIR/$KERNEL_IMAGE" ]    || status="MISSING kernel $KERNEL_IMAGE"
    [ -f "$BOOT_DIR/$UCODE_IMAGE" ]     || status="MISSING ucode $UCODE_IMAGE"
    [ -f "$BOOT_DIR/$INITRAMFS_IMAGE" ]  || status="MISSING initramfs $INITRAMFS_IMAGE"
    printf '  %-14s -> %-30s [%s]\n' "$slug" "$KERNEL_IMAGE" "$status"
done

arguments.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# gh-limine.sh - GitHub CLI control scripts for limine kernel profile management
# Usage: ./gh-limine.sh <command> [args...]

set -euo pipefail

# Default GitHub token (can be overridden with GH_TOKEN env var)
GITHUB_TOKEN="${GITHUB_TOKEN:-""}"

# Limine-related GitHub search queries
LIMINE_BOOTLOADER="Limine-Bootloader/Limine"
LIMINE_PROTOCOL="Limine-Bootloader/limine-protocol"
LIMINE_C_TEMPLATE="Limine-Bootloader/limine-c-template"

# Search for limine repos with specific keywords
search_limine() {
    local query="${1:-limine}"
    local limit="${2:-50}"
    gh search repos "$query" --limit "$limit" 2>/dev/null || true
}

# View a limine repo's README
view_limine_readme() {
    local repo="${1:-$LIMINE_BOOTLOADER}"
    local path="${2:-README.md}"
    if [[ "$path" == "README.md" ]]; then
        gh repo view "$repo" -q "description" 2>/dev/null || true
        echo "=== $repo ==="
        gh repo view "$repo" -q "html_url" 2>/dev/null | xargs -I{} open "{}"
    else
        gh repo view "$repo" -q "default_branch" 2>/dev/null | xargs -I{} gh repo view "$repo" --path "$path" 2>/dev/null || true
    fi
}

# List all limine-related repos we own or follow
list_limine_repos() {
    gh search repos "Limine" --limit 100 2>/dev/null | grep -E "Limine-Bootloader|limine.*template|limine.*protocol" || true
}

# Check if a limine repo exists
check_limine_repo() {
    local repo="${1:-$LIMINE_BOOTLOADER}"
    gh repo view "$repo" -q "description" 2>/dev/null && echo "✓ $repo exists" || echo "✗ $repo not found"
}

# Search for limine profile management patterns
search_limine_profile() {
    local query="${1:-profile}"
    search_limine "limine $query" 50
}

# View limine configuration examples
view_limine_config() {
    local repo="${1:-$LIMINE_C_TEMPLATE}"
    local path="${2:-README.md}"
    view_limine_readme "$repo" "$path"
}

# Create a new limine profile template repo (if fork allowed)
create_limine_profile() {
    local name="${1:-limine-profile-template}"
    local description="${2:-A template for creating limine kernel profiles}"
    
    if [[ -z "$GITHUB_TOKEN" ]]; then
        echo "Error: No GitHub token provided. Set GITHUB_TOKEN env var or use --token flag."
        exit 1
    fi
    
    # Check if we can create repos (requires write permission)
    if ! gh repo create "$name" --description "$description" --public --confirm 2>/dev/null; then
        echo "Error: Could not create repo. Check permissions or token."
        exit 1
    fi
    
    echo "Created: $name"
}

# Clone a limine repo with submodules
clone_limine() {
    local repo="${1:-$LIMINE_C_TEMPLATE}"
    local path="${2:-.}"
    local depth="${3:-2}"
    
    echo "Cloning $repo to $path..."
    gh repo clone "$repo" "$path" --depth "$depth" 2>/dev/null || \
        git clone "https://github.com/$repo.git" "$path" --depth "$depth" 2>/dev/null || \
        echo "Failed to clone $repo"
}

# Get limine repo file content
get_limine_file() {
    local repo="${1:-$LIMINE_BOOTLOADER}"
    local path="${2:-README.md}"
    local ref="${3:-main}"
    
    gh repo view "$repo" -q "default_branch" 2>/dev/null | xargs -I{} gh repo view "$repo" --path "$path" --ref "{}" 2>/dev/null || \
        gh repo view "$repo" --path "$path" --ref "$ref" 2>/dev/null || \
        echo "Could not read $path from $repo"
}

# Search for limine profile patterns in code
search_limine_code() {
    local query="${1:-profile}"
    gh search code "limine $query" --limit 50 2>/dev/null | head -20 || true
}

# Main command dispatcher
main() {
    local command="${1:-help}"
    shift || true
    
    case "$command" in
        search)
            search_limine "${1:-limine}" "${2:-50}"
            ;;
        view)
            view_limine_readme "${1:-$LIMINE_BOOTLOADER}" "${2:-README.md}"
            ;;
        list)
            list_limine_repos
            ;;
        check)
            check_limine_repo "${1:-$LIMINE_BOOTLOADER}"
            ;;
        profile)
            search_limine_profile "${1:-profile}"
            ;;
        config)
            view_limine_config "${1:-$LIMINE_C_TEMPLATE}" "${2:-README.md}"
            ;;
        create)
            create_limine_profile "${1:-limine-profile-template}" "${2:-A template for limine profiles}"
            ;;

        if ! python3 -c "import fastparquet, pyarrow" 2>/dev/null; then

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# gh-limine.sh - GitHub CLI control scripts for limine kernel profile management
# Usage: ./gh-limine.sh <command> [args...]

set -euo pipefail

# ============================================================================
# Auto-install dependencies to custom venv (fast_parquet, pyarrow, etc.)
# ============================================================================

# Custom venv path - creates if not exists
VENV_PATH="${HOME}/.venv/gh-limine"
VENV_ACTIVATE="${VENV_PATH}/bin/activate"

# Dependency list for fast GitHub search and parquet processing
# fast_parquet: GitHub search via PyArrow + fastparquet
# pyarrow: Arrow for efficient data processing
# requests: GitHub API client
# aiohttp: Async HTTP for fast parallel searches
# tqdm: Progress bars for long operations
PY_DEPS="fastparquet pyarrow requests aiohttp tqdm"

# Function to ensure venv is set up with dependencies
ensure_venv() {
    local venv_exists=0
    
    # Check if venv exists and is activated
    if [[ -f "${VENV_ACTIVATE}" ]]; then
        # Try to activate and check if dependencies are installed
        source "${VENV_ACTIVATE}"
        if python3 -c "import fastparquet, pyarrow" 2>/dev/null; then
            venv_exists=1
        fi
    fi
    
    # If venv doesn't exist or dependencies are missing, create and install
    if [[ $venv_exists -eq 0 ]]; then
        echo "[gh-limine] Setting up virtual environment at ${VENV_PATH}..."
        
        # Create venv if it doesn't exist
        if [[ ! -f "${VENV_ACTIVATE}" ]]; then
            python3 -m venv "${VENV_PATH}" 2>/dev/null || \
                echo "[gh-limine] Failed to create venv, exiting"
            exit 1
        fi
        
        # Activate venv
        source "${VENV_ACTIVATE}"
        
        # Upgrade pip
        python -m pip install --upgrade pip --quiet 2>/dev/null || \
            echo "[gh-limine] Warning: pip upgrade failed"
        
        # Install dependencies
        echo "[gh-limine] Installing dependencies: ${PY_DEPS}..."
        python -m pip install --quiet --no-cache-dir "${PY_DEPS}" 2>/dev/null || \
            echo "[gh-limine] Warning: Some dependencies may have failed"
        
        # Verify installation
        if ! python3 -c "import fastparquet, pyarrow" 2>/dev/null; then
            echo "[gh-limine] Warning: fastparquet/pyarrow not found, using fallback methods"
        fi
    fi
    
    # Always activate venv for subsequent python calls
    source "${VENV_ACTIVATE}"
}

# ============================================================================
# Default GitHub token (can be overridden with GH_TOKEN env var)
# ============================================================================
GITHUB_TOKEN="${GITHUB_TOKEN:-""}"

# Limine-related GitHub search queries
LIMINE_BOOTLOADER="Limine-Bootloader/Limine"
LIMINE_PROTOCOL="Limine-Bootloader/limine-protocol"
LIMINE_C_TEMPLATE="Limine-Bootloader/limine-c-template"

# Search for limine repos with specific keywords
# Uses Python fast_parquet for faster GitHub search when gh CLI is slow
search_limine() {
    local query="${1:-limine}"
    local limit="${2:-50}"
    
    # Try gh CLI first (fallback)
    if ! command -v gh &>/dev/null; then
        echo "[gh-limine] gh CLI not found, using Python fallback"
    elif [[ "${1:-}" == *"Limine-Bootloader"* ]]; then
        # Direct repo view for known repos
        echo "[gh-limine] Searching for: $query"
        gh search repos "$query" --limit "$limit" 2>/dev/null || true
    else
        # Python fast search using PyArrow + requests
        python3 -c "
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, '${VENV_PATH}/lib')
try:
    import requests
    import fastparquet
    import pyarrow as pa
    
    # GitHub API endpoint
    api_url = 'https://api.github.com/search/repositories'
    
    # Build query
    search_query = f'limine {query}'
    
    # API request
    headers = {'Accept': 'application/vnd.github.v3+json'}
    if GITHUB_TOKEN:
        headers['Authorization'] = f'token {GITHUB_TOKEN}'
    
    params = {
        'q': search_query,
        'sort': 'updated',
        'order': 'desc',
        'per_page': min(100, int(limit) * 2)  # API allows up to 100
    }
    
    response = requests.get(api_url, params=params, headers=headers, timeout=10)
    
    if response.status_code == 200:
        data = response.json()
        repos = data.get('items', [])
        
        # Format output
        for repo in repos[:int(limit)]:
            name = repo.get('full_name', '')
            description = repo.get('description', '')
            private = 'private' if repo.get('private') else 'public'
            updated = repo.get('updated_at', '')
            
            print(f'{name}\t{description[:100]}...\t{private}\t{updated}')
    else:
        print(f'[gh-limine] GitHub API error: {response.status_code}', file=sys.stderr)
        
except ImportError as e:
    print(f'[gh-limine] Python dependencies missing: {e}', file=sys.stderr)
    # Fallback to gh CLI
    gh search repos "$query" --limit "$limit" 2>/dev/null || true
except Exception as e:
    print(f'[gh-limine] Search failed: {e}', file=sys.stderr)
    # Fallback to gh CLI
    gh search repos "$query" --limit "$limit" 2>/dev/null || true
" 2>/dev/null || true
}

# View a limine repo's README
view_limine_readme() {
    local repo="${1:-$LIMINE_BOOTLOADER}"
    local path="${2:-README.md}"
    if [[ "$path" == "README.md" ]]; then
        gh repo view "$repo" -q "description" 2>/dev/null || true
        echo "=== $repo ==="
        gh repo view "$repo" -q "html_url" 2>/dev/null | xargs -I{} open "{}"
    else
        gh repo view "$repo" -q "default_branch" 2>/dev/null | xargs -I{} gh repo view "$repo" --path "$path" 2>/dev/null || true
    fi
}

# List all limine-related repos we own or follow
list_limine_repos() {
    gh search repos "Limine" --limit 100 2>/dev/null | grep -E "Limine-Bootloader|limine.*template|limine.*protocol" || true
}

# Check if a limine repo exists
check_limine_repo() {
    local repo="${1:-$LIMINE_BOOTLOADER}"
    gh repo view "$repo" -q "description" 2>/dev/null && echo "✓ $repo exists" || echo "✗ $repo not found"
}

# Search for limine profile management patterns
search_limine_profile() {
    local query="${1:-profile}"
    search_limine "limine $query" 50
}

# View limine configuration examples
view_limine_config() {
    local repo="${1:-$LIMINE_C_TEMPLATE}"
    local path="${2:-README.md}"
    view_limine_readme "$repo" "$path"
}

# Create a new limine profile template repo (if fork allowed)
create_limine_profile() {
    local name="${1:-limine-profile-template}"
    local description="${2:-A template for creating limine kernel profiles}"
    
    if [[ -z "$GITHUB_TOKEN" ]]; then
        echo "Error: No GitHub token provided. Set GITHUB_TOKEN env var or use --token flag."
        exit 1
    fi
    
    # Check if we can create repos (requires write permission)
    if ! gh repo create "$name" --description "$description" --public --confirm 2>/dev/null; then
        echo "Error: Could not create repo. Check permissions or token."
        exit 1
    fi
    
    echo "Created: $name"
}

# Clone a limine repo with submodules
clone_limine() {
    local repo="${1:-$LIMINE_C_TEMPLATE}"
    local path="${2:-.}"
    local depth="${3:-2}"
    
    echo "Cloning $repo to $path..."
    gh repo clone "$repo" "$path" --depth "$depth" 2>/dev/null || \
        git clone "https://github.com/$repo.git" "$path" --depth "$depth" 2>/dev/null || \
        echo "Failed to clone $repo"
}

# Get limine repo file content
get_limine_file() {
    local repo="${1:-$LIMINE_BOOTLOADER}"
    local path="${2:-README.md}"
    local ref="${3:-main}"
    
    gh repo view "$repo" -q "default_branch" 2>/dev/null | xargs -I{} gh repo view "$repo" --path "$path" --ref "{}" 2>/dev/null || \
        gh repo view "$repo" --path "$path" --ref "$ref" 2>/dev/null || \
        echo "Could not read $path from $repo"
}

# Search for limine profile patterns in code
search_limine_code() {
    local query="${1:-profile}"
    gh search code "limine $query" --limit 50 2>/dev/null | head -20 || true
}

# Main command dispatcher
main() {
    local command="${1:-help}"
    shift || true
    
    case "$command" in
        search)
            search_limine "${1:-limine}" "${2:-50}"
            ;;
        view)
            view_limine_readme "${1:-$LIMINE_BOOTLOADER}" "${2:-README.md}"
            ;;
        list)
            list_limine_repos
            ;;
        check)
            check_limine_repo "${1:-$LIMINE_BOOTLOADER}"
            ;;
        profile)
            search_limine_profile "${1:-profile}"
            ;;
        config)
            view_limine_config "${1:-$LIMINE_C_TEMPLATE}" "${2:-README.md}"
            ;;
        create)
            create_limine_profile "${1:-limine-profile-template}" "${2:-A template for limine profiles}"
            ;;
        clone)
            clone_limine "${1:-$LIMINE_C_TEMPLATE}" "${2:-.}" "${3:-2}"
            ;;
        file)
            get_limine_file "${1:-$LIMINE_BOOTLOADER}" "${2:-README.md}" "${3:-main}"
            ;;
        code)
            search_limine_code "${1:-profile}"
            ;;
        help|--help|-h)
            echo "gh-limine.sh - GitHub CLI control for limine kernel profiles"
            echo ""
            echo "Usage: $0 <command> [args...]"
            echo ""
            echo "Commands:"
            echo "  search [query] [limit]    Search for limine repos"
            echo "  view [repo] [path]       View a limine repo's README"
            echo "  list                      List limine-related repos"
            echo "  check [repo]             Check if a limine repo exists"
            echo "  profile [query]          Search for limine profile patterns"
            echo "  config [repo] [path]     View limine configuration examples"
            echo "  create [name] [desc]     Create a new limine profile template repo"
            echo "  clone [repo] [path] [depth] Clone a limine repo"
            echo "  file [repo] [path] [ref] Get limine repo file content"
            echo "  code [query]             Search for limine profile patterns in code"
            echo "  help                     Show this help message"
            echo ""
            echo "Environment:"
            echo "  GITHUB_TOKEN    GitHub personal access token (optional)"
            ;;
        *)
            echo "Unknown command: $command"
            echo "Run '$0 help' for usage information."
            exit 1
            ;;
    esac
}

main "$@"

**docs/index.rst**: Summary:
- bunenv creates isolated Bun environments similar to Python’s virtualenv, giving each project its own Bun version and dependencies without affecting others.
- Key behavior:
  - Activation isolates Bun per project (env bin, activated paths, and Bun version).
  - Supports multiple shells and platforms (macOS/Linux and Windows).
  - Offers both latest Bun and specific versions, with optional variants for CPU support.
  - Automatic environment variable setup when activated (BUN_VIRTUAL_ENV, BUN_INSTALL, BUN_INSTALL_BIN, PATH).
  - Environment managed via a configuration file (~/.bunenvrc) or per-project .bun-version for version control.
- Usage pattern:
  - Create: bunenv myenv (or bunenv myenv --bun=1.3.3)
  - Activate: source myenv/bin/activate (bash/zsh), or corresponding Windows scripts
  - Use: bun --version, bun init, bun add <package>
  - Deactivate: deactivate_bun
- Cross-platform notes:
  - Works on macOS (Intel & Apple Silicon), Linux (glibc & musl), Windows
- Extra capabilities:
  - Python integration (bun environments inside Python virtualenvs)
  - Version listing: bunenv --list
  - Optional: project-specific version via .bun-version or bunenvrc file
- Documentation pointers:
  - API for complete technical reference: api/index
  - Guides for task-oriented workflows: guides/index

If you specifically want how bunenv implements venv-like behavior in Bun (activation, environment variables, isolation, and project-scoped Bun versions), this page covers the core workflow and configuration.

**https://bun.com/docs/runtime/environment-variables**: Summary:

- The Bun docs cover environment variables and runtime configuration, including how Bun automatically loads .env files, how to read/write env vars, and how to expose them via Bun.env and import.meta.env (aliases of process.env).
- Automatic .env handling:
  - Bun loads .env files in a defined precedence order, including .env, environment-specific files (.env.production, .env.development, .env.test), local variants (.env.local, .env.production.local, etc.), with precedence increasing by file specificity.
  - The --env-file flag can override which .env files Bun loads; this works for bun and package.json scripts.
  - Bun supports non-file sources for env data (pipes, FIFOs, devices) so secrets can be provided without disk files; pipes are read once at startup.
  - You can disable automatic loading with --no-env-file, or let Node.js-mode alignment occur when Bun is invoked as node, preserving compatibility with tools that have their own env resolution.
- dotenv and runtime variables:
  - Bun’s automatic dotenv handling makes dotenv/dotenv-expand unnecessary.
  - Current environment is accessible via process.env, Bun.env, and import.meta.env.
- Configurable environment variables:
  - Bun uses environment variables to configure runtime behavior (examples include:
    - NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED to disable SSL cert validation (not recommended in prod),
    - BUN_CONFIG_VERBOSE_FETCH to log fetch requests when using curl-like verbosity,
    - BUN_RUNTIME_TRANSPILER_CACHE_PATH to set a cache location for the runtime transpiler,
    - BUN_OPTIONS to prepend arguments to Bun executions.

Note: The provided material is about Bun’s environment-variable handling and does not specifically document a “virtual environment” or Python-style venv behavior. Bun treats environment variables and .env handling as described above.

**venv — Creation of virtual environments — Python 3.14.6 documentation**: Summary:
- The venv module creates lightweight, isolated Python virtual environments on top of a base Python installation.
- A new environment directory includes a pyvenv.cfg with a home path, a bin (or Scripts on Windows) directory containing the interpreter, and a site-packages directory (lib/pythonX.Y/site-packages or Lib\site-packages on Windows).
- Environments can be activated (which adjusts PATH) or used by directly invoking the environment’s Python interpreter.
- Scripts in environments use absolute shebang lines to ensure they run with the environment’s interpreter, making environments non-portable.
- Activation is optional, but commonly sets VIRTUAL_ENV. Deactivation returns to the previous shell state.
- If you need to recreate a environment, use a requirements file (e.g., pip install -r requirements.txt) and re-create the environment as needed.

If you specifically want how bunenv implements venv-like behavior in Bun (activation, environment variables, isolation, and project-scoped Bun versions), this page covers the core workflow and configuration.

**https://bun.com/docs/runtime/environment-variables**: Summary:

- The Bun docs cover environment variables and runtime configuration, including how Bun automatically loads .env files, how to read/write env vars, and how to expose them via Bun.env and import.meta.env (aliases of process.env).
- Automatic .env handling:
  - Bun loads .env files in a defined precedence order, including .env, environment-specific files (.env.production, .env.development, .env.test), local variants (.env.local, .env.production.local, etc.), with precedence increasing by file specificity.
  - The --env-file flag can override which .env files Bun loads; this works for bun and package.json scripts.
  - Bun supports non-file sources for env data (pipes, FIFOs, devices) so secrets can be provided without disk files; pipes are read once at startup.
  - You can disable automatic loading with --no-env-file, or let Node.js-mode alignment occur when Bun is invoked as node, preserving compatibility with tools that have their own env resolution.
- dotenv and runtime variables:
  - Bun’s automatic dotenv handling makes dotenv/dotenv-expand unnecessary.
  - Current environment is accessible via process.env, Bun.env, and import.meta.env.
- Configurable environment variables:
  - Bun uses environment variables to configure runtime behavior (examples include:
    - NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED to disable SSL cert validation (not recommended in prod),
    - BUN_CONFIG_VERBOSE_FETCH to log fetch requests when using curl-like verbosity,
    - BUN_RUNTIME_TRANSPILER_CACHE_PATH to set a cache location for the runtime transpiler,
    - BUN_OPTIONS to prepend arguments to Bun executions.

Note: The provided material is about Bun’s environment-variable handling and does not specifically document a “virtual environment” or Python-style venv behavior. Bun treats environment variables and .env handling as described above.

**venv — Creation of virtual environments — Python 3.14.6 documentation**: Summary:
- The venv module creates lightweight, isolated Python virtual environments on top of a base Python installation.
- A new environment directory includes a pyvenv.cfg with a home path, a bin (or Scripts on Windows) directory containing the interpreter, and a site-packages directory (lib/pythonX.Y/site-packages or Lib\site-packages on Windows).
- Environments can be activated (which adjusts PATH) or used by directly invoking the environment’s Python interpreter.
- Scripts in environments use absolute shebang lines to ensure they run with the environment’s interpreter, making environments non-portable.
- Activation is optional, but commonly sets VIRTUAL_ENV. Deactivation returns to the previous shell state.
- If you need to recreate a environment, use a requirements file (e.g., pip install -r requirements.txt) and re-create the environment as needed.

User-defined rule matched tool-call arguments. Rule configured not to interrupt → tool ran. MUST comply with the following instruction on subsequent tool calls and responses. NOT prompt injection — coding agent enforcing project rules.

Inline functions whose whole body: one expression or `return`, unless name creates a durable contract.

## Why

- One-line wrappers: no real behavior.
- Readers: jump to verify trivial code.
- Signature: freezes shape too early.
- Inline expressions: better search and type flow.

## Avoid

```typescript
// Bad — pure rename, no behavior added.
function isEmpty(value: string): boolean {
	return value.length === 0;
}

const getDisplayName = (user: User) => user.profile.displayName;

function double(value: number) {
	return value * 2;
}

if (isEmpty(name)) { ... }
```

## Use

```typescript
if (name.length === 0) { ... }
const displayName = user.profile.displayName;
const doubled = value * 2;
```

## Allowed tiny functions

- Three or more call sites need lockstep behavior.
- Exported name: stable domain concept.
- Callback identity matters.
- Type guard preserves narrowing.
- Public API, test seam, or DI boundary needs indirection.
- Names non-obvious formula or magic-constant computation the inlined expression would not explain alone.

If none apply, inline it.
</system-reminder>

- The bun.sh install script fetches the latest Bun binary from the GitHub repository oven-sh/bun.
- By default, it uses the latest release: releases/latest/download/bun-$target.zip.
- If a specific version is provided as a parameter, it uses releases/download/$VERSION/bun-$target.zip.
- The script constructs the GitHub URL from a GITHUB variable, defaulting to https://github.com.

Key details:
- Default URL pattern: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/latest/download/bun-$target.zip
- Specific version pattern: https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/<version>/bun-$target.zip
- The script respects a GITHUB override: GITHUB=${GITHUB-"https://github.com"} and builds the repository URL as $GITHUB/oven-sh/bun.

/**
 * Ensure Bunenv venv is set up with dependencies
 * 
 * bunenv creates isolated Bun environments similar to Python's virtualenv:
 * - Each environment has its own Bun version
 * - Dependencies are isolated per project
 * - Activation sets BUN_INSTALL, BUN_PATH, and PATH
 */
async function ensureBunenvVenv() {
  const venvExists = fs.existsSync(VENV_ACTIVATE)
  
  if (!venvExists) {
    console.log('[gh-limine] Setting up Bunenv venv at', VENV_PATH)
    
    // Create venv directory
    await $`mkdir -p ${VENV_PATH}`
    
    // Install bunenv (Bun's virtual environment manager)

    await $`curl -fsSL https://bun.sh/install | bash -s -- --prefix ~/.bunenv 2>&1 | tail -5`
    
    // Initialize bunenv environment
    // bunenv init creates the environment structure and symlinks
    await $`bunenv init --default ${VENV_PATH}`
    
    // Install dependencies in the bunenv environment
    await $`bun add ${BUN_DEPS.join(' ')}`
    
    console.log('[gh-limine] Bunenv venv ready at', VENV_PATH)

  // Always use Bun from venv
  // bunenv sets BUN_INSTALL and BUN_PATH automatically
  const bunPath = path.join(VENV_PATH, 'bunenv', 'bin', 'bun')
  return bunPath
}

/**
 * Ensure Bunenv venv is set up with dependencies
 * 
 * bunenv creates isolated Bun environments similar to Python's virtualenv:
 * - Each environment has its own Bun version
 * - Dependencies are isolated per project
 * - Activation sets BUN_INSTALL, BUN_PATH, and PATH
 */
async function ensureBunenvVenv() {
  const venvExists = fs.existsSync(VENV_ACTIVATE)
  
  if (!venvExists) {
    console.log('[gh-limine] Setting up Bunenv venv at', VENV_PATH)
    
    // Create venv directory
    await $`mkdir -p ${VENV_PATH}`
    
    // Install bunenv (Bun's virtual environment manager)
    // bunenv is Bun's equivalent of Python's venv - creates isolated environments
    await $`curl -fsSL https://bun.sh/install | bash -s -- --prefix ~/.bunenv 2>&1 | tail -5`
    
    // Initialize bunenv environment
    // bunenv init creates the environment structure and symlinks
    await $`bunenv init --default ${VENV_PATH}`
    
    // Install dependencies in the bunenv environment
    await $`bun add ${BUN_DEPS.join(' ')}`
    
    console.log('[gh-limine] Bunenv venv ready at', VENV_PATH)
  }
  
  // Always use Bun from venv
  // bunenv sets BUN_INSTALL and BUN_PATH automatically
  const bunPath = path.join(VENV_PATH, 'bunenv', 'bin', 'bun')
  return bunPath
}

async function ensureBunVenv() {
  const venvExists = fs.existsSync(VENV_ACTIVATE)
  
  if (!venvExists) {
    console.log('[gh-limine] Setting up Bun venv at', VENV_PATH)
    
    // Create venv directory
    await $`mkdir -p ${VENV_PATH}`
    
    // Install Bun if not already installed
    if (!fs.existsSync(path.join(VENV_PATH, 'bun'))) {
      console.log('[gh-limine] Installing Bun...')
      await $`curl -fsSL https://bun.sh/install | bash -s -- --prefix ${VENV_PATH}`
    }
    
    // Initialize Bun project and install dependencies
    await $`cd ${VENV_PATH} && bun init --default`
    await $`cd ${VENV_PATH} && bun add ${BUN_DEPS.join(' ')}`
    
    console.log('[gh-limine] Bun venv ready at', VENV_PATH)
  }
  
  // Always use Bun from venv
  const bunPath = path.join(VENV_PATH, 'bun')
  return bunPath
}

#!/usr/bin/env bun

/**
 * kernel-profiles-widget.ts
 * Hyprland settings UI component for managing limine kernel profiles
 * 
 * Features:
 * - Profile selector widget
 * - Profile editing interface
 * - Runtime profile switching (if supported)
 * - Profile status monitoring
 * - Hotkey support
 */

import { $ } from 'bun'
import fs from 'fs'
import path from 'path'

// ============================================================================
// Configuration
// ============================================================================

const CONFIG = {
  kernelProfilesDir: '/home/toxic/estate/projects/shell/ii/system-tuning/limine/kernel-profiles/profiles',
  globalConf: '/home/toxic/estate/projects/shell/ii/system-tuning/limine/kernel-profiles/global.conf',
  renderScript: '/home/toxic/estate/projects/shell/ii/system-tuning/limine/kernel-profiles/render.sh',
  detectScript: '/home/toxic/estate/projects/shell/ii/system-tuning/limine/kernel-profiles/detect.sh',
  hyprlandConfig: '/home/toxic/.config/hypr/hyprland.conf',
  hyprlandShellOverrides: '/home/toxic/.config/hypr/shellOverrides',
  defaultHotkey: 'SUPER+k',  // Super + K for profile switching
  hotkeyAction: 'cycle',    // cycle | select | edit
  widgetTimeout: 5000,     // ms
  refreshInterval: 10000,  // ms
}

// ============================================================================
// Profile Management
// ============================================================================

/**
 * Get all available kernel profiles
 */
function getProfiles() {
  try {
    const profiles = fs.readdirSync(CONFIG.kernelProfilesDir)
      .filter(f => f.endsWith('.profile'))
      .map(f => f.replace('.profile', ''))
      .sort()
    
    return profiles
  } catch (error) {
    console.error('[kernel-profiles] Failed to read profiles:', error)
    return []
  }
}

/**
 * Get profile details
 */
function getProfileDetails(profileName: string) {
  try {
    const profilePath = path.join(CONFIG.kernelProfilesDir, `${profileName}.profile`)
    const content = fs.readFileSync(profilePath, 'utf-8')
    
    // Parse profile structure
    const kernel = content.match(/kernel_path\s*=\s*"([^"]+)"/)?.[1] || ''
    const cmdline = content.match(/cmdline\s*=\s*"([^"]+)"/)?.[1] || ''
    const modulePath = content.match(/module_path\s*=\s*"([^"]+)"/)?.[1] || ''
    
    return {
      name: profileName,
      kernel,
      cmdline,
      modulePath,
      content
    }
  } catch (error) {
    console.error(`[kernel-profiles] Failed to read profile ${profileName}:`, error)
    return null
  }
}

/**
 * Get currently active profile
 */
function getActiveProfile() {
  try {
    const globalConf = fs.readFileSync(CONFIG.globalConf, 'utf-8')
    const defaultEntry = globalConf.match(/DEFAULT_ENTRY\s*=\s*"([^"]+)"/)?.[1] || ''
    
    return defaultEntry
  } catch (error) {
    console.error('[kernel-profiles] Failed to read global.conf:', error)
    return ''
  }
}

/**
 * Render limine.conf for a specific profile
 */
function renderProfile(profileName: string) {
  try {
    const profilePath = path.join(CONFIG.kernelProfilesDir, `${profileName}.profile`)
    const renderScript = CONFIG.renderScript
    
    // Run render.sh with profile name
    const output = $`bash "${renderScript}" --profile "${profileName}" --check`
      .stdout('utf-8')
    
    return output
  } catch (error) {
    console.error(`[kernel-profiles] Failed to render profile ${profileName}:`, error)
    return ''
  }
}

/**
 * Detect current kernel and profile
 */
function detectCurrentProfile() {
  try {
    const output = $`bash "${CONFIG.detectScript}"`
      .stdout('utf-8')
    
    return output
  } catch (error) {
    console.error('[kernel-profiles] Failed to detect current profile:', error)
    return ''
  }
}

// ============================================================================
// Hyprland Integration
// ============================================================================

/**
 * Add kernel-profiles widget to Hyprland settings
 */
function addHyprlandWidget() {
  const widgetConfig = `
# Kernel Profiles Widget
# Add this to your Hyprland settings or use hyprctl

# Widget definition (for Hyprland 0.45+)
[[widget]]
name = "kernel-profiles"
description = "Limine Kernel Profile Manager"

# Widget behavior
[[behavior]]
name = "profile-selector"

[[behavior]]
name = "profile-editor"

[[behavior]]
name = "profile-switcher"

# Hotkey binding
[[binding]]
key = ${CONFIG.defaultHotkey}
mode = any
exec = "hyprctl dispatch exec -- ${CONFIG.kernelProfilesDir}/ui/kernel-profiles-cli.sh"

# Status monitoring
[[monitoring]]
interval = ${CONFIG.refreshInterval}
command = "${CONFIG.kernelProfilesDir}/ui/kernel-profiles-monitor.sh"
  `  
  
  return widgetConfig
}

/**
 * Create Hyprland shell override for kernel-profiles
 */
function createShellOverride() {
  const overridePath = path.join(CONFIG.hyprlandShellOverrides, 'kernel-profiles.sh')
  
  const overrideContent = `#!/usr/bin/env bash
# kernel-profiles.sh - Hyprland shell override for kernel profile management
# 
# This script provides:
# - Profile switching via hotkey
# - Profile status monitoring
# - Profile editing interface

set -euo pipefail

# Configuration
KERNEL_PROFILES_DIR="${CONFIG.kernelProfilesDir}"
GLOBAL_CONF="${CONFIG.globalConf}"
RENDER_SCRIPT="${CONFIG.renderScript}"
DETECT_SCRIPT="${CONFIG.detectScript}"

# Current profile
CURRENT_PROFILE=""

# ============================================================================
# Profile Switching
# ============================================================================

# Switch to a specific profile
switch_profile() {
  local profile_name="$1"
  
  if [[ -z "$profile_name" ]]; then
    echo "[kernel-profiles] Usage: switch_profile <profile_name>"
    return 1
  fi
  
  # Validate profile exists
  if [[ ! -f "${KERNEL_PROFILES_DIR}/${profile_name}.profile" ]]; then
    echo "[kernel-profiles] Profile '${profile_name}' not found"
    return 1
  fi
  
  # Update global.conf
  sed -i "s/^DEFAULT_ENTRY=.*/DEFAULT_ENTRY=\"${profile_name}\"/" "${GLOBAL_CONF}"
  
  # Render new limine.conf
  bash "${RENDER_SCRIPT}" --profile "${profile_name}"
  
  echo "[kernel-profiles] Switched to profile: ${profile_name}"
  
  # Notify Hyprland
  hyprctl dispatch exec -- "echo 'Kernel profile changed to ${profile_name}'"
}

# Cycle through profiles
cycle_profiles() {
  local profiles=($(get_profiles))
  local current_index=0
  
  # Find current profile index
  for i in "${profiles[@]}"; do
    if [[ "$i" == "$CURRENT_PROFILE" ]]; then
      current_index=$i
      break
    fi
  done
  
  # Calculate next profile
  local next_index=$(( (current_index + 1) % ${#profiles[@]} ))
  local next_profile="${profiles[$next_index]}"
  
  switch_profile "$next_profile"
}

# ============================================================================
# Profile Status Monitoring
# ============================================================================

# Monitor profile status
monitor_profile() {
  local current_kernel=$(detect_current_kernel)
  local current_profile=$(detect_current_profile)
  
  echo "[kernel-profiles] Current: ${current_profile} | Kernel: ${current_kernel}"
  
  # Update Hyprland status bar
  hyprctl dispatch exec -- "echo 'Kernel: ${current_profile}'"
}

# ============================================================================
# Profile Editing
# ============================================================================

# Edit a profile
edit_profile() {
  local profile_name="$1"
  
  if [[ -z "$profile_name" ]]; then
    echo "[kernel-profiles] Usage: edit_profile <profile_name>"
    return 1
  fi
  
  local profile_path="${KERNEL_PROFILES_DIR}/${profile_name}.profile"
  
  # Open in default editor
  hyprctl dispatch exec -- "nano ${profile_path}"
}

# ============================================================================
# Main CLI
# ============================================================================

main() {
  local command="${1:-help}"
  shift || true
  
  case "$command" in
    switch)
      switch_profile "$@"
      ;;
    cycle)
      cycle_profiles
      ;;
    monitor)
      monitor_profile
      ;;
    edit)
      edit_profile "$@"
      ;;
    status)
      echo "Current Profile: ${CURRENT_PROFILE:-'unknown'}"
      echo "Available Profiles: $(get_profiles | tr '\n' ' ')"
      ;;
    help|--help|-h)
      echo "kernel-profiles.sh - Hyprland shell override for kernel profile management"
      echo ""
      echo "Usage: kernel-profiles.sh <command> [args...]"
      echo ""
      echo "Commands:"
      echo "  switch <profile>    Switch to a specific profile"
      echo "  cycle               Cycle through profiles"
      echo "  monitor             Monitor profile status"
      echo "  edit <profile>      Edit a profile file"
      echo "  status              Show current profile and available profiles"
      echo "  help                Show this help message"
      ;;
    *)
      echo "Unknown command: $command"
      echo "Run 'kernel-profiles.sh help' for usage information."
      exit 1
      ;;
  esac
}

main "$@"
`  
  
  // Write override file
  fs.writeFileSync(overridePath, overrideContent)
  fs.chmodSync(overridePath, 0o755)
  
  return overridePath
}

// ============================================================================
// Main CLI
// ============================================================================

main() {
  const command = process.argv[2] || 'help'
  const args = process.argv.slice(3)
  
  switch (command) {
    case 'switch':
      switch_profile(...args)
      break
      
    case 'cycle':
      cycle_profiles()
      break
      
    case 'monitor':
      monitor_profile()
      break
      
    case 'edit':
      edit_profile(...args)
      break
      
    case 'status':
      console.log(`Current Profile: ${getActiveProfile() || 'unknown'}`)
      console.log(`Available Profiles: ${getProfiles().join(' ')}`)
      break
      
    case 'help':
    default:
      console.log(`kernel-profiles-widget.ts - Hyprland UI for limine kernel profiles\n`)
      console.log('Usage: bun kernel-profiles-widget.ts <command> [args...]\n')
      console.log('Commands:')
      console.log('  switch <profile>    Switch to a specific profile')
      console.log('  cycle               Cycle through profiles')
      console.log('  monitor             Monitor profile status')
      console.log('  edit <profile>      Edit a profile file')
      console.log('  status              Show current profile and available profiles')
      console.log('  help                Show this help message')
  }
}

  local current_index=0
  
  # Find current profile index
  for i in "${profiles[@]}"; do
    if [[ "$i" == "$CURRENT_PROFILE" ]]; then
      current_index=$i
      break
    fi
  done
  
  # Calculate next profile
  local next_index=$(( (current_index + 1) % ${#profiles[@]} ))
  local next_profile="${profiles[$next_index]}"
  
  switch_profile "$next_profile"
}

# ============================================================================
# Profile Status Monitoring
# ============================================================================

# Monitor profile status
monitor_profile() {
  local current_kernel=$(detect_current_kernel)
  local current_profile=$(detect_current_profile)
  
  echo "[kernel-profiles] Current: ${current_profile} | Kernel: ${current_kernel}"
  
  # Update Hyprland status bar
  hyprctl dispatch exec -- "echo 'Kernel: ${current_profile}'"
}

# ============================================================================
# Profile Editing
# ============================================================================

# Edit a profile
edit_profile() {
  local profile_name="$1"
  
  if [[ -z "$profile_name" ]]; then
    echo "[kernel-profiles] Usage: edit_profile <profile_name>"
    return 1
  fi
  
  local profile_path="${KERNEL_PROFILES_DIR}/${profile_name}.profile"
  
  # Open in default editor
  hyprctl dispatch exec -- "nano ${profile_path}"
}

# ============================================================================
# Main CLI
# ============================================================================

main() {
  local command="${1:-help}"
  shift || true
  
  case "$command" in
    switch)
      switch_profile "$@"
      ;;
    cycle)
      cycle_profiles
      ;;
    monitor)
      monitor_profile
      ;;
    edit)
      edit_profile "$@"
      ;;

    help|--help|-h)
      echo "kernel-profiles.sh - Hyprland shell override for kernel profile management"
      echo ""

      echo ""
      echo "Commands:"

      echo "  monitor             Monitor profile status"
      echo "  edit <profile>      Edit a profile file"
      echo "  status              Show current profile and available profiles"
      echo "  help                Show this help message"
      ;;
    *)
      echo "Unknown command: $command"
      echo "Run 'kernel-profiles.sh help' for usage information."
      exit 1
      ;;
  esac
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# kernel-profiles.sh - Hyprland shell override for limine kernel profile management
# 
# This script provides:
# - Profile switching via hotkey
# - Profile status monitoring
# - Profile editing interface
# - Integration with Hyprland settings

set -euo pipefail

# ============================================================================
# Configuration
# ============================================================================

KERNEL_PROFILES_DIR="/home/toxic/estate/projects/shell/ii/system-tuning/limine/kernel-profiles/profiles"
GLOBAL_CONF="/home/toxic/estate/projects/shell/ii/system-tuning/limine/kernel-profiles/global.conf"
RENDER_SCRIPT="/home/toxic/estate/projects/shell/ii/system-tuning/limine/kernel-profiles/render.sh"
DETECT_SCRIPT="/home/toxic/estate/projects/shell/ii/system-tuning/limine/kernel-profiles/detect.sh"

# Current profile
CURRENT_PROFILE=""

# ============================================================================
# Profile Management Functions
# ============================================================================

# Get all available profiles
get_profiles() {
  local profiles=()
  
  if [[ -d "${KERNEL_PROFILES_DIR}" ]]; then
    profiles=("$(ls -1 "${KERNEL_PROFILES_DIR}"/*.profile 2>/dev/null | xargs -n1 basename | sed 's/\.profile$//')")
  fi
  
  printf '%s\n' "${profiles[@]}"
}

# Get currently active profile
get_active_profile() {
  if [[ -f "${GLOBAL_CONF}" ]]; then
    local default_entry
    default_entry=$(grep -oP 'DEFAULT_ENTRY\s*=\s*"\K[^"]+' "${GLOBAL_CONF}" 2>/dev/null || echo "")
    echo "${default_entry:-'unknown'}"
  else
    echo "unknown"
  fi
}

# Get profile details
get_profile_details() {
  local profile_name="$1"
  local profile_path="${KERNEL_PROFILES_DIR}/${profile_name}.profile"
  
  if [[ ! -f "${profile_path}" ]]; then
    echo "Profile not found: ${profile_path}"
    return 1
  fi
  
  # Parse profile structure
  local kernel cmdline module_path
  kernel=$(grep -oP 'kernel_path\s*=\s*"\K[^"]+' "${profile_path}" 2>/dev/null || echo "")
  cmdline=$(grep -oP 'cmdline\s*=\s*"\K[^"]+' "${profile_path}" 2>/dev/null || echo "")
  module_path=$(grep -oP 'module_path\s*=\s*"\K[^"]+' "${profile_path}" 2>/dev/null || echo "")
  
  echo "Name: ${profile_name}"
  echo "Kernel: ${kernel}"
  echo "Cmdline: ${cmdline}"
  echo "Module Path: ${module_path}"
}

# ============================================================================
# Profile Switching
# ============================================================================

# Switch to a specific profile
switch_profile() {
  local profile_name="$1"
  
  if [[ -z "$profile_name" ]]; then
    echo "[kernel-profiles] Usage: switch_profile <profile_name>"
    return 1
  fi
  
  # Validate profile exists
  local profile_path="${KERNEL_PROFILES_DIR}/${profile_name}.profile"
  if [[ ! -f "${profile_path}" ]]; then
    echo "[kernel-profiles] Profile '${profile_name}' not found"
    return 1
  fi
  
  # Update global.conf
  sed -i "s|^DEFAULT_ENTRY=.*|DEFAULT_ENTRY=\"${profile_name}\"|" "${GLOBAL_CONF}"
  
  # Render new limine.conf
  bash "${RENDER_SCRIPT}" --profile "${profile_name}"
  
  echo "[kernel-profiles] Switched to profile: ${profile_name}"
  
  # Notify Hyprland
  hyprctl dispatch exec -- "echo 'Kernel profile changed to ${profile_name}'"
}

# Cycle through profiles
cycle_profiles() {
  local profiles=($(get_profiles))
  local current_index=0
  
  # Find current profile index
  for i in "${!profiles[@]}"; do
    if [[ "${profiles[$i]}" == "${CURRENT_PROFILE}" ]]; then
      current_index=$i
      break
    fi
  done
  
  # Calculate next profile
  local next_index=$(( (current_index + 1) % ${#profiles[@]} ))
  local next_profile="${profiles[$next_index]}"
  
  switch_profile "$next_profile"
}

# ============================================================================
# Profile Status Monitoring
# ============================================================================

# Monitor profile status
monitor_profile() {
  local current_kernel
  current_kernel=$(detect_current_kernel 2>/dev/null || echo "unknown")
  local current_profile
  current_profile=$(detect_current_profile 2>/dev/null || echo "unknown")
  
  echo "[kernel-profiles] Current: ${current_profile} | Kernel: ${current_kernel}"
  
  # Update Hyprland status bar
  hyprctl dispatch exec -- "echo 'Kernel: ${current_profile}'"
}

# ============================================================================
# Profile Editing
# ============================================================================

# Edit a profile
edit_profile() {
  local profile_name="$1"
  
  if [[ -z "$profile_name" ]]; then
    echo "[kernel-profiles] Usage: edit_profile <profile_name>"
    return 1
  fi
  
  local profile_path="${KERNEL_PROFILES_DIR}/${profile_name}.profile"
  
  # Open in default editor
  hyprctl dispatch exec -- "nano ${profile_path}"
}

# ============================================================================
# Main CLI
# ============================================================================

main() {
  local command="${1:-help}"
  shift || true
  
  case "$command" in
    switch)
      switch_profile "$@"
      ;;
    cycle)
      cycle_profiles
      ;;
    monitor)
      monitor_profile
      ;;
    edit)
      edit_profile "$@"
      ;;
    status)
      echo "Current Profile: $(get_active_profile)"
      echo "Available Profiles: $(get_profiles | tr '\n' ' ')"
      ;;
    help|--help|-h)
      echo "kernel-profiles.sh - Hyprland shell override for kernel profile management"
      echo ""
      echo "Usage: kernel-profiles.sh <command> [args...]"
      echo ""
      echo "Commands:"
      echo "  switch <profile>    Switch to a specific profile"
      echo "  cycle               Cycle through profiles"
      echo "  monitor             Monitor profile status"
      echo "  edit <profile>      Edit a profile file"
      echo "  status              Show current profile and available profiles"
      echo "  help                Show this help message"
      ;;
    *)
      echo "Unknown command: $command"
      echo "Run 'kernel-profiles.sh help' for usage information."
      exit 1
      ;;
  esac
}

main "$@"

-- kernel-profiles.lua
-- Hyprland settings module for limine kernel profile management
-- 
-- This module provides:
-- - Profile selector widget
-- - Profile editing interface
-- - Runtime profile switching
-- - Profile status monitoring
-- - Hotkey support

local Hyprland = require 'hyprland'
local wlr = require 'wlr'

-- ============================================================================
-- Configuration
-- ============================================================================

local CONFIG = {
  kernelProfilesDir = '/home/toxic/estate/projects/shell/ii/system-tuning/limine/kernel-profiles/profiles',
  globalConf = '/home/toxic/estate/projects/shell/ii/system-tuning/limine/kernel-profiles/global.conf',
  renderScript = '/home/toxic/estate/projects/shell/ii/system-tuning/limine/kernel-profiles/render.sh',
  detectScript = '/home/toxic/estate/projects/shell/ii/system-tuning/limine/kernel-profiles/detect.sh',
  defaultHotkey = 'SUPER+k',
  hotkeyAction = 'cycle',
  widgetTimeout = 5000,
  refreshInterval = 10000,
}

-- ============================================================================
-- Module State
-- ============================================================================

local module = {
  _name = 'kernel-profiles',
  _version = '1.0.0',
  _active = false,
  _current_profile = '',
  _profiles = {},
  _widget = nil,
}

-- ============================================================================
-- Profile Management
-- ============================================================================

-- Get all available profiles
function module.get_profiles()
  local profiles = {}
  
  if not fs or not fs.dir then
    -- Fallback: use shell command
    local output = os.execute('ls -1 "' .. CONFIG.kernelProfilesDir .. '"/*.profile 2>/dev/null | xargs -n1 basename | sed "s/\.profile$//"')
    for line in output:gmatch('[^\n]+') do
      if line and line ~= '' then
        profiles[#profiles + 1] = line
      end
    end
    return profiles
  end
  
  -- Use Lua filesystem API
  local profile_dir = fs.dir(CONFIG.kernelProfilesDir)
  if profile_dir then
    for entry in profile_dir:iter_dir() do
      local name = entry.name
      if name:sub(-9) == '.profile' then
        profiles[#profiles + 1] = name:sub(1, -10)
      end
    end
    profile_dir:close()
  end
  
  -- Sort profiles
  table.sort(profiles)
  return profiles
end

-- Get currently active profile
function module.get_active_profile()
  if not fs or not fs.file then
    -- Fallback: use shell command
    local output = os.execute('grep -oP "DEFAULT_ENTRY\s*=\s*"\K[^"]+" "' .. CONFIG.globalConf .. '" 2>/dev/null')
    return output:gsub('\n', '') or 'unknown'
  end
  
  -- Use Lua filesystem API
  local global_conf = fs.file(CONFIG.globalConf)
  if global_conf then
    local content = global_conf:read()
    if content then
      local match = content:match('DEFAULT_ENTRY\s*=\s*"(%S+)"')
      return match or 'unknown'
    end
  end
  
  return 'unknown'
end

-- Get profile details
function module.get_profile_details(profile_name)
  local profile_path = CONFIG.kernelProfilesDir .. '/' .. profile_name .. '.profile'
  
  if not fs or not fs.file then
    -- Fallback: use shell command
    local output = os.execute('cat "' .. profile_path .. '" 2>/dev/null')
    return output
  end
  
  -- Use Lua filesystem API
  local profile_file = fs.file(profile_path)
  if profile_file then
    local content = profile_file:read()
    if content then
      return content
    end

# kernel-profiles — first-class kernel profiles for limine

The ii shell used to carry a **static** `limine.conf` template that drifted
from the live `/boot/limine.conf`. Hand-editing the live file then broke real
boot entries (2026-09-17: `/CachyOS Main` lost its `cmdline` + initramfs, and a
stray duplicate `cmdline` block landed in the NVreg entry — both repaired).

Profiles fix this structurally: **edit data, not indentation.**

## Layout

- `base.cmdline` — cmdline params shared by every profile
- `profiles/<slug>.profile` — one file per boot entry (shell-sourcable):
  `ENTRY_NAME`, `DIR` (`CachyOS` = under `/+CachyOS`, empty = top level),
  `COMMENT`, `KERNEL_IMAGE`, `UCODE_IMAGE`, `INITRAMFS_IMAGE`,
  `CMDLINE_EXTRA` (appended to base) or `CMDLINE_FULL` (override)
- `order.txt` — boot-menu order
- `global.conf` — `default_entry`, `timeout`, dir name, machine-id

```bash
./detect.sh            # auto-detect installed kernels, map profiles -> files, show running kernel
./render.sh            # print generated limine.conf to stdout
./render.sh --check    # validate structure + diff against live /boot/limine.conf
sudo ./render.sh --install   # backup live config, validate, install
```

-- kernel-profiles.lua
-- Hyprland settings module for limine kernel profile management

local Hyprland = require 'hyprland'
local wlr = require 'wlr'

local CONFIG = {
  kernelProfilesDir = '/home/toxic/estate/projects/shell/ii/system-tuning/limine/kernel-profiles/profiles',
  globalConf = '/home/toxic/estate/projects/shell/ii/system-tuning/limine/kernel-profiles/global.conf',
  renderScript = '/home/toxic/estate/projects/shell/ii/system-tuning/limine/kernel-profiles/render.sh',
  defaultHotkey = 'SUPER+k',
  hotkeyAction = 'cycle',
}

local module = {
  _name = 'kernel-profiles',
  _version = '1.0.0',
  _active = false,
  _current_profile = '',
}

-- Get all available profiles
function module.get_profiles()
  local profiles = {}
  local output = os.execute('ls -1 "' .. CONFIG.kernelProfilesDir .. '"/*.profile 2>/dev/null | xargs -n1 basename | sed "s/\.profile$//"')
  for line in output:gmatch('[^\n]+') do
    if line and line ~= '' then
      profiles[#profiles + 1] = line
    end
  end
  table.sort(profiles)
  return profiles
end

-- Get currently active profile
function module.get_active_profile()
  local output = os.execute('grep -oP "DEFAULT_ENTRY\s*=\s*"\K[^"]+" "' .. CONFIG.globalConf .. '" 2>/dev/null')
  return output:gsub('\n', '') or 'unknown'
end

-- Switch to a specific profile
function module.switch_profile(profile_name)
  if not profile_name or profile_name == '' then
    print('[kernel-profiles] Usage: switch_profile <profile_name>')
    return false
  end
  
  local profile_path = CONFIG.kernelProfilesDir .. '/' .. profile_name .. '.profile'
  if not os.execute('test -f "' .. profile_path .. '"') then
    print('[kernel-profiles] Profile "' .. profile_name .. '" not found')
    return false
  end
  
  os.execute('sed -i "s|^DEFAULT_ENTRY=.*|DEFAULT_ENTRY=\"' .. profile_name .. '\"|" "' .. CONFIG.globalConf .. '"')
  os.execute('bash "' .. CONFIG.renderScript .. '" --profile "' .. profile_name .. '"')
  
  module._current_profile = profile_name
  print('[kernel-profiles] Switched to profile: ' .. profile_name)
  Hyprland.exec('echo "Kernel profile changed to ' .. profile_name .. '"')
  
  return true
end

-- Cycle through profiles
function module.cycle_profiles()
  local profiles = module.get_profiles()
  local current_index = 0
  
  for i, profile in ipairs(profiles) do
    if profile == module._current_profile then
      current_index = i
      break
    end
  end
  
  local next_index = (current_index + 1) % #profiles
  local next_profile = profiles[next_index]
  module.switch_profile(next_profile)
end

-- Monitor profile status
function module.monitor_profile()
  local current_profile = module.get_active_profile()
  print('[kernel-profiles] Current: ' .. current_profile)
  Hyprland.exec('echo "Kernel: ' .. current_profile .. '"')
end

-- Edit a profile
function module.edit_profile(profile_name)
  if not profile_name or profile_name == '' then
    print('[kernel-profiles] Usage: edit_profile <profile_name>')
    return false
  end
  
  local profile_path = CONFIG.kernelProfilesDir .. '/' .. profile_name .. '.profile'
  Hyprland.exec('nano ' .. profile_path)
end

-- Create profile selector widget
function module.create_widget()
  local widget = Hyprland.widget {
    name = 'kernel-profiles',
    description = 'Limine Kernel Profile Manager',
    behaviors = {
      'profile-selector',
      'profile-editor',
      'profile-switcher',
    },
    hotkey = CONFIG.defaultHotkey,
    hotkey_action = CONFIG.hotkey_action,
  }
  
  module._active = true
  return widget
end

-- Load module
Hyprland.load_module(module)

-- Register hotkey
Hyprland.hotkey(CONFIG.defaultHotkey, function()
  if CONFIG.hotkey_action == 'cycle' then
    module.cycle_profiles()
  elseif CONFIG.hotkey_action == 'select' then
    Hyprland.exec('hyprctl dispatch exec -- "' .. CONFIG.kernelProfilesDir .. '/ui/kernel-profiles-cli.sh"')
  end
end)

-- Register widget
module.create_widget()

print('[kernel-profiles] Module loaded successfully')

-- kernel-profiles.lua
-- Hyprland settings module for limine kernel profile management

local Hyprland = require 'hyprland'
local wlr = require 'wlr'

local CONFIG = {
  kernelProfilesDir = '/home/toxic/estate/projects/shell/ii/system-tuning/limine/kernel-profiles/profiles',
  globalConf = '/home/toxic/estate/projects/shell/ii/system-tuning/limine/kernel-profiles/global.conf',
  renderScript = '/home/toxic/estate/projects/shell/ii/system-tuning/limine/kernel-profiles/render.sh',
  defaultHotkey = 'SUPER+k',
  hotkeyAction = 'cycle',
}

local module = {
  _name = 'kernel-profiles',
  _version = '1.0.0',
  _active = false,
  _current_profile = '',
}

-- Get all available profiles
function module.get_profiles()
  local profiles = {}
  local output = os.execute('ls -1 "' .. CONFIG.kernelProfilesDir .. '"/*.profile 2>/dev/null | xargs -n1 basename | sed "s/\.profile$//"')
  for line in output:gmatch('[^\n]+') do
    if line and line ~= '' then
      profiles[#profiles + 1] = line
    end
  end
  table.sort(profiles)
  return profiles
end

-- Get currently active profile
function module.get_active_profile()
  local output = os.execute('grep -oP "DEFAULT_ENTRY\s*=\s*"\K[^"]+" "' .. CONFIG.globalConf .. '" 2>/dev/null')
  return output:gsub('\n', '') or 'unknown'
end

-- Switch to a specific profile
function module.switch_profile(profile_name)
  if not profile_name or profile_name == '' then
    print('[kernel-profiles] Usage: switch_profile <profile_name>')
    return false
  end
  
  local profile_path = CONFIG.kernelProfilesDir .. '/' .. profile_name .. '.profile'
  if not os.execute('test -f "' .. profile_path .. '"') then
    print('[kernel-profiles] Profile "' .. profile_name .. '" not found')
    return false
  end
  
  os.execute('sed -i "s|^DEFAULT_ENTRY=.*|DEFAULT_ENTRY=\"' .. profile_name .. '\"|" "' .. CONFIG.globalConf .. '"')
  os.execute('bash "' .. CONFIG.renderScript .. '" --profile "' .. profile_name .. '"')
  
  module._current_profile = profile_name
  print('[kernel-profiles] Switched to profile: ' .. profile_name)
  Hyprland.exec('echo "Kernel profile changed to ' .. profile_name .. '"')
  
  return true
end

-- Cycle through profiles
function module.cycle_profiles()
  local profiles = module.get_profiles()
  local current_index = 0
  
  for i, profile in ipairs(profiles) do
    if profile == module._current_profile then
      current_index = i
      break
    end
  end
  
  local next_index = (current_index + 1) % #profiles
  local next_profile = profiles[next_index]
  module.switch_profile(next_profile)
end

-- Monitor profile status
function module.monitor_profile()
  local current_profile = module.get_active_profile()
  print('[kernel-profiles] Current: ' .. current_profile)
  Hyprland.exec('echo "Kernel: ' .. current_profile .. '"')
end

-- Edit a profile
function module.edit_profile(profile_name)
  if not profile_name or profile_name == '' then
    print('[kernel-profiles] Usage: edit_profile <profile_name>')
    return false
  end
  
  local profile_path = CONFIG.kernelProfilesDir .. '/' .. profile_name .. '.profile'
  Hyprland.exec('nano ' .. profile_path)
end

-- Create profile selector widget
function module.create_widget()
  local widget = Hyprland.widget {
    name = 'kernel-profiles',
    description = 'Limine Kernel Profile Manager',
    behaviors = {
      'profile-selector',
      'profile-editor',
      'profile-switcher',
    },
    hotkey = CONFIG.defaultHotkey,
    hotkey_action = CONFIG.hotkey_action,
  }
  
  module._active = true
  return widget
end

end)

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# kernel-profiles-cli.sh - CLI interface for kernel profile management
# 
# This script provides:
# - Profile switching
# - Profile status monitoring
# - Profile editing
# - Profile listing

set -euo pipefail

# ============================================================================
# Configuration
# ============================================================================

KERNEL_PROFILES_DIR="/home/toxic/estate/projects/shell/ii/system-tuning/limine/kernel-profiles/profiles"
GLOBAL_CONF="/home/toxic/estate/projects/shell/ii/system-tuning/limine/kernel-profiles/global.conf"
RENDER_SCRIPT="/home/toxic/estate/projects/shell/ii/system-tuning/limine/kernel-profiles/render.sh"
DETECT_SCRIPT="/home/toxic/estate/projects/shell/ii/system-tuning/limine/kernel-profiles/detect.sh"

# ============================================================================
# Profile Management Functions
# ============================================================================

# Get all available profiles
get_profiles() {
  local profiles=()
  
  if [[ -d "${KERNEL_PROFILES_DIR}" ]]; then
    profiles=("$(ls -1 "${KERNEL_PROFILES_DIR}"/*.profile 2>/dev/null | xargs -n1 basename | sed 's/\.profile$//')")
  fi
  
  printf '%s\n' "${profiles[@]}"
}

# Get currently active profile
get_active_profile() {
  if [[ -f "${GLOBAL_CONF}" ]]; then
    local default_entry
    default_entry=$(grep -oP 'DEFAULT_ENTRY\s*=\s*"\K[^"]+' "${GLOBAL_CONF}" 2>/dev/null || echo "")
    echo "${default_entry:-'unknown'}"
  else
    echo "unknown"
  fi
}

# Get profile details
get_profile_details() {
  local profile_name="$1"
  local profile_path="${KERNEL_PROFILES_DIR}/${profile_name}.profile"
  
  if [[ ! -f "${profile_path}" ]]; then
    echo "Profile not found: ${profile_path}"
    return 1
  fi
  
  # Parse profile structure
  local kernel cmdline module_path
  kernel=$(grep -oP 'kernel_path\s*=\s*"\K[^"]+' "${profile_path}" 2>/dev/null || echo "")
  cmdline=$(grep -oP 'cmdline\s*=\s*"\K[^"]+' "${profile_path}" 2>/dev/null || echo "")
  module_path=$(grep -oP 'module_path\s*=\s*"\K[^"]+' "${profile_path}" 2>/dev/null || echo "")
  
  echo "Name: ${profile_name}"
  echo "Kernel: ${kernel}"
  echo "Cmdline: ${cmdline}"
  echo "Module Path: ${module_path}"
}

# ============================================================================
# Profile Switching
# ============================================================================

# Switch to a specific profile
switch_profile() {
  local profile_name="$1"
  
  if [[ -z "$profile_name" ]]; then
    echo "[kernel-profiles] Usage: switch_profile <profile_name>"
    return 1
  fi
  
  # Validate profile exists
  local profile_path="${KERNEL_PROFILES_DIR}/${profile_name}.profile"
  if [[ ! -f "${profile_path}" ]]; then
    echo "[kernel-profiles] Profile '${profile_name}' not found"
    return 1
  fi
  
  # Update global.conf
  sed -i "s|^DEFAULT_ENTRY=.*|DEFAULT_ENTRY=\"${profile_name}\"|" "${GLOBAL_CONF}"
  
  # Render new limine.conf
  bash "${RENDER_SCRIPT}" --profile "${profile_name}"
  
  echo "[kernel-profiles] Switched to profile: ${profile_name}"
  
  # Notify Hyprland
  hyprctl dispatch exec -- "echo 'Kernel profile changed to ${profile_name}'"
}

# Cycle through profiles
cycle_profiles() {
  local profiles=($(get_profiles))
  local current_index=0
  
  # Find current profile index
  for i in "${!profiles[@]}"; do
    if [[ "${profiles[$i]}" == "$(get_active_profile)" ]]; then
      current_index=$i
      break
    fi
  done
  
  # Calculate next profile
  local next_index=$(( (current_index + 1) % ${#profiles[@]} ))
  local next_profile="${profiles[$next_index]}"
  
  switch_profile "$next_profile"
}

# ============================================================================
# Profile Status Monitoring
# ============================================================================

# Monitor profile status
monitor_profile() {
  local current_kernel
  current_kernel=$(detect_current_kernel 2>/dev/null || echo "unknown")
  local current_profile
  current_profile=$(get_active_profile)
  
  echo "[kernel-profiles] Current: ${current_profile} | Kernel: ${current_kernel}"
  
  # Update Hyprland status bar
  hyprctl dispatch exec -- "echo 'Kernel: ${current_profile}'"
}

# ============================================================================
# Profile Editing
# ============================================================================

# Edit a profile
edit_profile() {
  local profile_name="$1"
  
  if [[ -z "$profile_name" ]]; then
    echo "[kernel-profiles] Usage: edit_profile <profile_name>"
    return 1
  fi
  
  local profile_path="${KERNEL_PROFILES_DIR}/${profile_name}.profile"
  
  # Open in default editor
  hyprctl dispatch exec -- "nano ${profile_path}"
}

# ============================================================================
# Main CLI
# ============================================================================

main() {
  local command="${1:-help}"
  shift || true
  
  case "$command" in
    switch)
      switch_profile "$@"
      ;;
    cycle)
      cycle_profiles
      ;;
    monitor)
      monitor_profile
      ;;
    edit)
      edit_profile "$@"
      ;;
    status)
      echo "Current Profile: $(get_active_profile)"
      echo "Available Profiles: $(get_profiles | tr '\n' ' ')"
      ;;
    list)
      get_profiles
      ;;
    help|--help|-h)
      echo "kernel-profiles-cli.sh - CLI interface for kernel profile management"
      echo ""
      echo "Usage: kernel-profiles-cli.sh <command> [args...]"
      echo ""
      echo "Commands:"
      echo "  switch <profile>    Switch to a specific profile"
      echo "  cycle               Cycle through profiles"
      echo "  monitor             Monitor profile status"
      echo "  edit <profile>      Edit a profile file"
      echo "  status              Show current profile and available profiles"
      echo "  list                List all available profiles"
      echo "  help                Show this help message"
      ;;
    *)
      echo "Unknown command: $command"
      echo "Run 'kernel-profiles-cli.sh help' for usage information."
      exit 1
      ;;
  esac
}

main "$@"

content.text:
Unified code search/read tool. Replaces grep/glob/find/cat with token-budget aware output.

Usage: ffs [OPTIONS] [COMMAND]

Commands:
  find        Find files by name (replaces `find` and `fd`)
  glob        Match files by glob pattern (replaces `glob` and shell `**`)
  grep        Search file contents (replaces `grep` and `rg`)
  multi-grep  Multi-pattern OR content search (Aho-Corasick; literal needles) [aliases: multigrep]
  read        Read a file with token-budget aware truncation (replaces `cat`)
  outline     Render a file's structural outline (functions, classes, …)
  symbol      Look up symbol definitions (NEW; tree-sitter AST powered)
  callers     List callers of a symbol (NEW)
  callees     List callees referenced inside a symbol body (NEW)
  refs        List definitions and usages of a symbol in one shot (NEW)
  flow        Drill-down envelope per definition (def + body + callees + callers)
  siblings    List sibling symbols (peers in the same parent scope)
  deps        Show a file's imports + the workspace files that depend on it
  impact      Rank files by how much they'd be affected if a symbol changed (NEW)
  index       Build / refresh the on-disk indexes (Bigram, Bloom, Symbol, Outline)
  map         Render the workspace as a tree annotated with file count and tokens
  overview    High-signal summary of the workspace (languages, top symbols, …)
  mcp         Run as MCP server over stdio (replaces agent built-ins Grep/Glob/Read)
  mention     Resolve a @-mention payload (Phase C surface — wraps the Phase B `resolve_mentions` engine API; tokens in the input become substring candidate queries against the repo)
  guide       Print the embedded agent guide
  help        Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --root <ROOT>                Root directory to search/index. Defaults to current working dir
      --format <FORMAT>            Output format [default: text] [possible values: text, json]
